title: Strike of the Deir el-Medina workmen
summary: In year 29 of Ramesses III, the royal tomb workmen of Deir el-Medina stopped work when their grain rations were withheld. They left the village for the Theban necropolis and the temples, struck again after a payment, and a last stoppage is reported for January. The Turin Strike Papyrus, from the tomb scribe Amunnakht, records the dispute.

uncertainty.note: Sources disagree: Papyrus Stories dates year 29 to ca. 1155 BCE (astronomical -1154), while the Museo Egizio gives Ramesses III as 1187-1157 BC, which would put year 29 earlier; start_minus_years 30 reaches the Museo reign. End is the January after the first November stoppage.

as_recorded.value: Year 29 (Ramesses III), second month of the Inundation, day 10

as_recorded.calendar: Egyptian regnal year; BCE as given

where.historical_name: Deir el-Medina, the workmen's village by the Theban necropolis, Egypt under Ramesses III

importance.justification: A documented work stoppage by state workers over unpaid rations, recorded in an administrative papyrus.
